classification.difficultyReason: Combines absolute-value transformations with reciprocal graph features, including a repeated zero and reflected vertical asymptotes.

content.prompt: The diagram shows the graph of $y=f(x)$. Sketch the graph of the following.

spec.description: Ungrid­ded axes with x and y labels; curve touches the origin at a local maximum, dips below the positive x-axis, crosses at the labelled intercept 2, and continues with arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative graph only. The supplied zeroes are x=0 and x=2. Bézier control coordinates describe drawing proportions, not additional numerical givens or an asserted formula.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied question figure; contains no transformed graph.

inlines.text: Three positive branches, with vertical asymptotes
Reflect the portions below the x-axis above it, then reciprocate the ordinates.

answer.worked:
Reflect the portions of $y=f(x)$ below the $x$-axis to obtain $y=|f(x)|$. Its zeroes remain $0$ and $2$.

Taking reciprocals makes both zeroes vertical asymptotes. All remaining ordinates are positive. The graph rises without bound on both sides of each vertical asymptote; between $0$ and $2$, the maximum of $|f(x)|$ becomes a positive minimum. The outer branches approach $y=0$. There are no axis intercepts.

spec.description: Three positive branches. The middle branch has a positive minimum; the outer branches approach the x-axis. The y-axis is the pole x=0; a dashed guide marks x=2.
spec.mathematics: Domain excludes 0 and 2. Both one-sided limits at each pole are positive infinity. No numerical minimum or formula is asserted.

inlines.text: An even graph with vertical asymptotes
Keep the right half, reflect it across the y-axis, then reciprocate the ordinates.

answer.worked:
To obtain $y=f(|x|)$, discard the original left half, keep the right half, and reflect a copy across the $y$-axis. The resulting zeroes are $-2$, $0$ and $2$.

Taking reciprocals preserves the signs and turns these zeroes into vertical asymptotes. The two inner branches are negative and tend to $-\infty$ at both ends. The outer branches are positive, tend to $+\infty$ beside $x=\pm2$, and approach $y=0$ as $|x|$ increases. The graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis and has no axis intercepts.

spec.mathematics: Domain excludes -2, 0 and 2. At x=0 both one-sided limits are negative infinity. Each outer pole has opposite signs on its two sides. Curve heights and extrema are qualitative.
